messages:
incident-bot: Paging: High 5xx rate from inference proxy in us-west-2a (affected route: /v1/generate). Customers: 2 high-traffic customers reporting increased errors. Auto-escalation to SRE.
alex_gonzalez: seeing a spike in proxy 502/504s in the metrics dashboard, p95 up ~150ms -> 800ms, p99 much worse. rolling window shows error rate started ~10:40 UTC.
mira_zhang: confirmed from traces — NLB target group shows repeated target health checks failing for a subset of instances in us-west-2a. NLB logs show TCP resets to the instance ENI.
oncall-sre: grabbing the oncall. I'll check instance side and host-level metrics. tagging infra oncall. @infra-bot can you surface instance attach/ENI errors in the last 30m?
infra-bot: ENI attach failures: 27 events in us-west-2a between 10:38-10:46 UTC. Error code: AttachNetworkInterfaceThrottled (rate exceeded) in cloud-provider logs. Also seeing higher tx_error counts on eni-*-g5 hosts.
alex_gonzalez: that matches the proxy logs — connection errors come from a small subset of hosts that recently scaled up. Could be hot-path burst + ENI attach rate limit + NLB not rebalancing.
mira_zhang: quick mitigation: mark unhealthy targets for the NLB target group to drain traffic away from the problematic hosts. Can we do a rapid reroute to cross-AZ targets?
oncall-sre: initiating NLB target deregister for the 6 suspect instances in us-west-2a (manual drain). Command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn tg-abc --targets Id=i-07f...`
incident-bot: Automated action: scale-up of cross-az proxy fleet in us-west-2b initiated (policy: emergency-redirect). New instances should be registered within ~3 minutes.
product-ops: customer-impact note: two customers reported degraded throughput; one saw 40% request failures. We should prepare an incident banner and post to status after we stabilize.
alex_gonzalez: after deregistering the bad targets, error rate dropped ~60% within 90s. p50/p95 back to normal for most routes, but some residual 5xx from long-lived connections.
mira_zhang: root cause hypothesis: a recent spike in scale-up caused many ENI attach attempts; AWS rate-limited ENI attachments in that AZ, which led to partial connectivity for newly created proxies. NLB health check failures followed, causing client 502s.
oncall-sre: next steps: (1) keep the affected instances cordoned and trigger instance replacement once ENI quotas recovered, (2) implement safer scale-up with staggered ENI attach windows and pre-warmed ENI pool for that AZ, (3) add NLB slow-attach circuit-breaker to avoid flapping. I've opened a follow-up ticket.
product-ops: agreed. Customer comms draft: short outage summary + mitigation + ETA for postmortem. I'll prepare and sync with comms.
incident-bot: Handoff: oncall-sre -> alex_gonzalez for follow-up remediation and postmortem. Paging cleared; monitored to stable at 10:50 UTC.
oncall-sre: leaving notes in runbook: affected AZ us-west-2a, symptom ENI attach throttling -> NLB target health flaps -> proxy 502s. Customer impact: elevated 5xx for two customers between 10:38–10:50 UTC, peak failure rate ~42%.
alex_gonzalez: will take the follow-up. saving logs: `s3://redwood-incident-logs/7970001234/` — includes NLB logs, instance syslogs, cloud provider ENI events. Creating P0 follow-up with remediation owner and timeline.
mira_zhang: recommend adding a metric alert for ENI attach throttles per AZ in infra monitoring so we can act before NLB health collapses. Also suggest a playbook addition for rapid cross-AZ reroute.
oncall-sre: leaving channel, follow-up assigned. :white_check_mark:
